---
title: "Native Start migration runbook"
description: "How each web app except apps/web moves to TanStack Start + Void + Vite+ on Cloudflare Workers: ownership, the bridge, basePath readiness, acceptance gates, held publication, direct cutover with an instant rollback, and the post-deploy watch."
updatedAt: '2026-10-25'
audience: developers
---

Every web app except `apps/web` moves to its own TanStack Start + Void + Vite+
Worker on Cloudflare. `apps/web` now has a separately scheduled Web 1 candidate; all existing Web routes remain on Next.js.
The retired `apps/tanstack-web` tree is not part of this program and is not
revived. Current hosting (Vercel, or Next.js/OpenNext Workers) stays canonical
for an app until its explicit cutover PR merges.

## Mastermind build artifact delivery

`mastermind-cloudflare.yaml` builds the native Worker on GitHub and uploads
`mastermind-cutover-<source SHA>` with `mastermind-native.tar.gz`. The app-owned
job requires emitted-runtime smoke after uploading and has no publication steps. The archive contains the emitted Worker,
assets, Wrangler config, deployment pointer and exact-source hash receipt.
Discover its config with `scripts/ci/mastermind-native-artifact.py config` after
restoring the archive with that helper's `restore` command. Set
`MASTERMIND_SOURCE_SHA` to the artifact's full source SHA for either operation.

This build-only delivery does not admit production publication. Mastermind's
security review and owner-only authentication remain in force. The release
operator must preserve the canonical host's Access policy and capture the
existing route and immutable rollback target before switching it. Auth/data
adapter changes belong in separate PRs from build wiring.

## Web candidate pre-publication requirements

Before publishing the separate Web 1 staging profile,
verify that its Worker and staging Next origin share a staging-only
`TRUSTED_PROXY_ORIGIN_SECRET` that is distinct from production's. Origin-IP
proofs are not bound to an environment or audience. Compare SHA-256 fingerprints
privately through the approved secret store before publication and after either
key rotates; equal or unavailable fingerprints hold publication. Keep only the
verification receipt in private release evidence. The candidate has no configured
production fingerprint, so runtime admission does not enforce this distinction.

Verify the exact upstream's Vercel team, project and immutable deployment ID
before forwarding credentials or proofs. The `tuturuuu-*.vercel.app` hostname
prefix is not bound to our Vercel team. The required staging Supabase identity
attestation fails closed after forwarding, and does not replace that ownership
check. These requirements must land before staging is published; source approval
alone does not authorize publication or provisioning.

## Staging workflow protection preflight

The Web staging publisher and reusable native staging publisher run
`scripts/ci/wave1-staging-preflight.mjs` before any job references a deployment
environment or provider secret. The preflight checks both
`wave1-web-next-staging` and `wave1-web-staging` for Web, or
`wave1-<app>-staging` for a native app. Each environment must already exist,
have required reviewers, and allow only the exact `main` branch through a custom
branch policy. Tags, wildcard patterns, additional policies, missing fields and
API errors refuse the run. The preflight never creates environments.

Repository `WAVE1_STAGING_PUBLISH_ENABLED` must equal the string `true`.
Web also requires a nonempty `WEB_STAGING_NEXT_ADMISSION`; native publication
requires a nonempty `WAVE1_STAGING_PUBLICATION_ADMISSION`. Existing admission
checks still validate the exact source and artifact. Empty or unset variables
refuse publication before a protected job starts.

The preflight uses only the automatic GitHub token, with `actions: read` for
the environment API and `contents: read` for checkout. Provisioning or changing
protection remains the release owner's responsibility. Protection is checked at
run admission; owners must preserve it throughout the run.

Verify this gate with
`node --test scripts/ci/wave1-staging-preflight.test.mjs`. Mocked API tests cover
missing environments, reviewers and branch restrictions; workflow tests enforce
the transitive dependency on preflight for every protected or secret-bearing job.

## Ownership

- **One integration writer per app.** Only that lane edits the app's runtime,
  Worker entry, Vite/Void config and owning workflow. Other lanes hand changes
  to it.
- **`next/*` only through `@tuturuuu/start-bridge`.** App source keeps its App
  Router modules; the Vite preset aliases `next/*` to the bridge. Do not copy
  shims into the app. If the bridge lacks something, extend the package
  (additive within its frozen v0 contract) rather than forking it locally.
- **Registries are generated.** `start-bridge-routes check` runs in the app's CI
  and fails on any `route.*`/`page.*` that is not generated, owned by named
  native code, or ignored with a reason.
- Domain libraries stay framework-independent. Inject request identity,
  storage, navigation and localization at the adapter.

### Request-scoped satellite authentication

`@tuturuuu/satellite/auth-request` exposes the shared satellite session and
profile helpers without importing Next request globals. Native adapters pass the
current `request`, the registered `targetApp`, and a request-bound
`getSupabaseSessionUser` callback. That callback must use the existing verified
Supabase session resolver; a caller-provided actor ID is not authentication.
App-session verification retains its target scope and takes precedence over the
Supabase fallback for session and user reads. Profile reads retain the existing
central API forwarding and fallback behavior.

Next callers keep `@tuturuuu/satellite/auth`, which obtains headers and the
Supabase resolver from the Next adapter. The shared Start preset already owns
the Next aliases, RSC/SSR ports and mount handling; apps should reuse those
ports rather than create alternate identity or navigation implementations.
`packages/satellite/src/auth-request.test.ts` covers explicit request/target
forwarding, rejected identities, profile fallback and interleaved requests;
`auth.test.ts` covers the Next adapter.

### Provider requests that forbid redirects

Workers supports `redirect: 'manual'` and `redirect: 'follow'`. The Fetch-standard
`redirect: 'error'` mode throws before dispatch on Workers. For credential-bearing
provider requests that must not follow redirects, use `manual` and reject
`opaqueredirect` and every 3xx before reading a response body or refreshing
credentials. Do not forward `Location` or retry a redirected mutation.

Calendar's Graph sync transport retains its single-attempt cancellation budget.
Mail's provider transport permits only its existing GET-on-401 credential refresh;
its OAuth token/profile and SNS certificate readers require a direct successful
response. Focused tests cover direct success, redirect and opaque-response denial,
and the existing retry limits. Verify the transport in local workerd with synthetic
identity boundaries and an outbound interceptor; record every attempted host and
require that a redirect never reaches its destination. Provider and production
acceptance remain separate from this local check. See the
[Workers Request reference](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/request/).

## basePath readiness

Each app must serve both its subdomain and `tuturuuu.com/<app>` from the same
source. `tuturuuu.com/<app>` is the app root; product marketing moves to
`/products/<app>`. Build with `TUTURUUU_BASE_PATH=/<app>` to produce the
path-mounted variant. The bridge supplies the asset base, server-function base,
router basepath, Location rewriting, base-aware links and auth return URLs.

Under a base, every app uses the **one shared `tuturuuu.com` root session**,
with no per-app cookie names or paths (user decisions of 2026-10-25 and
2026-10-26: one session for every app, held server-side in an `HttpOnly`
cookie). Mounted apps read that session and derive their per-app claims in
memory; they never write or clear `tuturuuu_app_session*` or Supabase session
cookies (the mounted no-writer guard).
Users who already hold the root session stay signed in at cutover; only users
without one sign in once on the apex. There is no cross-host token handoff from
the subdomain. Subdomain hosts keep their host-only app-session cookies until
they only redirect.

## Gates before cutover

The generated binding-type harness extends the owning app's base tsconfig and
checks its full source graph with `noEmit` and `allowImportingTsExtensions`.
The latter admits explicit `.ts` imports in Worker configuration without emitting
unbundled JavaScript. Keep inherited includes, type roots and paths intact;
binding incompatibilities must still fail. Verify the harness with
`python3 scripts/ci/native-binding-type-harness.test.py`, which compiles a
fixture with extension imports and rejects an incompatible binding type.

An app is cutover-ready only with all of the following for the exact commit:

1. Exact-commit CI green: unit tests, type-check, lint, the registry check, a
   real `vp build`, and the app's owning native workflow.
2. Sealed emitted-Worker acceptance: the built artifact is hashed, its emitted
   config is validated, the emitted runtime suite passes, and a fresh restore
   of the same archive passes the same suite with unchanged bytes.
3. Staging acceptance on the owner-provisioned staging Worker: authentication
   and session refresh, MFA, workspace permissions, bilingual hydration, the
   app's primary flows, and both the subdomain and `/<app>` mounts.
4. A rollback record: the immutable prior deployment (artifact or deployment
   ID) and the captured routing (routes, custom domains and DNS records) that
   cutover replaces.

## Held publication and cutover

Production publication stays **held per app** in `productionPublicationPolicy`
(`tuturuuu.ci.ts`) until an explicit cutover PR admits that app. Deleting a
hold never admits publication. A cutover PR names the exact artifact, the
routing change and the rollback record, and merges only with the gates above.

Approvals:

- DNS, zone, canonical-route and staging-provider changes need release-authority
  approval.
- Production database migrations are auto-approved by the fleet; they still need
  an exact-SQL security review, green CI and staging, and the gated
  `supabase-production.yaml` workflow. The bridge itself needs none.

## Direct cutover

Every app, including Tasks, Contacts and Finance, cuts over **directly** once
the gates above pass. There are no staged canaries or traffic percentages.

**Before the flip**, prepare and record an instant one-step rollback:

- the immutable prior deployment (the current Vercel deployment ID, or the
  prior Worker version), confirmed still serving;
- the captured routing it replaces (routes, custom domains, DNS records and
  any zone rules), with the exact command or API call that restores it;
- who executes the rollback during the watch.

**The flip** changes only the routing for that one app, in one step.

**After the flip:**

1. Run the post-deploy smoke within minutes: sign-in and session refresh,
   the app's primary flows, both the subdomain and `/<app>` mounts, and a
   check that responses carry `x-tuturuuu-runtime: native`.
2. Watch for 30–60 minutes. Roll back immediately, without waiting for a
   diagnosis, on any regression:

   | Signal | Rollback when |
   | --- | --- |
   | Server errors | 5xx rate rises above the prior deployment's baseline |
   | Authentication | Any auth loop, unexpected sign-out, or rise in auth failures |
   | Latency | p95 TTFB clearly above the prior baseline |
   | Client errors | Client error rate rises above the prior baseline |
   | Smoke | Any smoke check fails |

3. File a cutover report: the exact artifact and commit, the routing change,
   smoke and watch results with the baselines used, and either the confirmed
   cutover or the rollback with its cause.

## Rollback

Rolling back an app restores the captured routing to the immutable prior
deployment in one step. Never delete the prior deployment or its routing record until the native
runtime has served all traffic through a full release cycle.

### Rewise anonymous smoke diagnostics

Rewise's centralized auth proxy handles signed-out `/` before its native page.
The redirect targets `https://tuturuuu.com/login` with an app-session `returnUrl`
pointing to `/verify-token?nextUrl=...` on the Rewise origin. The native `/login`
page instead supplies the Rewise root as its return target. Check the full return
target as well as the login origin and path; retain unknown-host, apex-host,
missing-secret and outbound-isolation probes.

The Rewise server-artifact scanner permits original `process.env.NODE_ENV`
branches in validated v3 source maps. Executable files still reject that text,
and both raw and JSON-decoded source maps reject development-secret prefixes.
Run `node --test apps/rewise/cloudflare/server-artifact-scan.test.mjs
apps/rewise/cloudflare/central-login-redirect.test.mjs` for the build-free
regressions. These fixtures do not replace the emitted-Worker smoke gate.

### Artifact profile and runtime fixture contracts

Infrastructure native builds remove server sourcemaps and their executable
references before sealing. Client maps remain available.
`cloudflare/server-artifact.test.mjs` covers idempotent preparation and rejection
of executable development branches and JSON-escaped development-secret prefixes.
The production runtime fixture measures executable and gzip bytes and rejects
server maps above 60 MiB and scripts above 64 MiB. Hosted upload and startup
acceptance remain separate gates.

Infrastructure production qualification preserves the emitted producer metadata
and validates the production Worker name, public app/Web URLs, production
`NODE_ENV`, required-secret flag and disabled source-map upload. The production
profile is explicit on config, seal and pack; staging remains the default.
`infrastructure-native-artifact.test.py` covers profile selection and refusal.

Infrastructure's `/api/build-info` requires an authenticated root-workspace
member with infrastructure permission and sufficient MFA assurance. Production
qualification uses `cloudflare/build-info-admin.runtime.mjs` to check the real
bundled SHA through that boundary, including anonymous, membership, permission
and MFA refusals. Never make the endpoint public to satisfy a publication probe.
The Infrastructure branch of `wave1-native-runtime.mjs` runs that fixture with
`cloudflare/production.runtime.mjs`, then verifies the artifact hashes again.
The production fixture checks the canonical app/Web URLs, disabled public preview
and source-map uploads, signed-out login redirects, static bytes and unknown-host
404 responses with outbound requests denied. Its explicit
`INFRASTRUCTURE_ARTIFACT_PROFILE=production` selector keeps the staging runtime
suite separate. Unknown paths on the canonical host redirect signed-out users to
`/login?next=...`; use an unadmitted host for the host-fence 404 probe.

Rewise removes server maps before doctor and seal; Mind prepares server output
as part of its native build. Client maps remain available. Their production-seal
regressions verify that executable development defaults are still rejected.
Mind runtime fixtures use an isolated first-party abuse-guard service with real
SQLite Durable Objects, bounded outbound denial and disposable bindings.
Pay runtime expectations include the canonical staging cookie domain and retain
foreign-domain and origin refusal checks.

Build identity must come from generated source metadata in the emitted Worker,
never a test responder returning an expected SHA. Qualify only the mounts admitted
by the selected app profile; a rejected apex host remains a negative control.

### Running the artifact gate on a local build

`scripts/ci/local-native-gate.sh <app> <artifact-script> <source-sha-env>
[--profile <name>] [--out <dir>]` runs config, seal, verify and the emitted-config
receipt on the checked-out commit's built app, writing only to a private temp
directory. The receipt helper requires `realpath(RUNNER_TEMP)` to equal
`RUNNER_TEMP`; on macOS the default temp directories sit under the
`/var` to `/private/var` symlink, which reports the receipt as `unavailable`
for a healthy build. The helper creates its temp directory under a canonical path.

When an app's workflow rewrites `dist/server/wrangler.json` (for example the
production Worker config step in `learn-cloudflare.yaml`), run that step's script
unchanged before the gate. Retyping it by hand can leave a malformed config that
the seal rejects. Meet uses `scripts/ci/verify-meet-start-output.js` with an
in-tree seal and is not covered by the helper.

Meet's dry-run gate also measures encoded and compressed sourcemaps before
invoking Wrangler. Cloudflare rejects encoded maps above 60 MiB with error
10021 even when the emitted Worker starts locally. Meet retains map uploads
and omits embedded dependency source text in its SSR output; mappings and
source paths remain available. Check the `meet_source_maps` receipt alongside
the emitted Worker startup probes. A dry run alone does not certify either
hosted upload acceptance or production behavior. The focused upload regression
coverage lives in `scripts/ci/wave1-native-upload-limits.test.mjs`.

Wave-1 production seals carry no server source maps. Publication configs set
`upload_source_maps: false`, and `wave1-native-artifact.mjs prepare` removes
every `.map` file and external `sourceMappingURL` reference under the Worker
module root before taking the inventory. The seal therefore covers exactly the
modules Wrangler uploads, and `verify` refuses a production seal that still
holds either. Calendar's production build emits about 91 MiB of server maps,
above the 60 MiB encoded limit. Mail emits about 25 MiB. Staging seals keep
their maps, and client assets are not modified. The `serverSourceMapsRemoved`
log line reports the removed count and bytes. Regression coverage lives in
`scripts/ci/wave1-native-source-maps.test.mjs`.

### Finance held-profile host acceptance

Finance's native staging and production qualification profiles admit only their
selected subdomain root. `apps/finance/start-bridge.config.ts` overrides the
generated Worker defaults with `mountHosts: []` and `unknownHost: 'reject'`.
The shared mount resolver applies that override before dispatching any route.
Consequently, `/api/build-info` on the selected root returns the real generated
source identity, while both `tuturuuu.com/api/build-info` and
`tuturuuu.com/finance/api/build-info` return 404. Other profiles' roots and
unlisted hosts remain rejected. The original emitted-Worker runtime suite
asserts this matrix in its raw Host subtest.

The basePath readiness target above does not enable a held profile's apex mount.
A positive mounted acceptance requires an explicitly admitted mount profile and
its session, origin and cookie-isolation evidence. A 404 on an unadmitted apex
host is a host-fence result, not evidence that the root build-info route is
missing. Keep production publication held until the cutover gates are met.

### Finance production publication qualification

Build Finance with `VITE_FINANCE_NATIVE_PROFILE=production` and the production
public Supabase publishable key. The profile pins `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` and
`FINANCE_APP_URL` to `https://finance.tuturuuu.com` and the Web origin to
`https://tuturuuu.com`; conflicting public URLs fail before bundling. Build its
workspace suppliers, generate exact-source build metadata, then run
`bun run build:cloudflare` in `apps/finance`. The ordinary package `build`
command produces the separate Next deployment.

Run the Finance artifact helper's `config` validation with the production
profile and a writable `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, then prepare the shared production seal
with `wave1-native-artifact.mjs`. Run `wave1-native-runtime.mjs` and the
publisher's token-free `dry-run` with a canonical `RUNNER_TEMP`. The publication
profile disables source-map upload. Finance omits embedded supplier source text
from SSR and RSC maps, retaining mappings and paths. Retained diagnostic maps
are distinct from uploaded maps; keep their total below 60 MiB and retain the exact CLI raw/gzip
measurements from the dry run. Hosted startup CPU still requires provider
acceptance.

With an emitted production build, run the additional focused probes:

```sh
CI=true CI_SOURCE_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" VITE_FINANCE_NATIVE_PROFILE=production \
  node --test apps/finance/cloudflare/production-publication.runtime.mjs
```

The probes require signed-out `/` and a protected workspace to return 307 to
central `/login`, with a Finance `/verify-token` return URL preserving `nextUrl`.
They check actual static bytes, a missing static asset's 404, outbound isolation,
the server-map budget and forbidden development defaults. They use disposable
runtime bindings and do not qualify real sign-in, session refresh or production
supplier access. Compare the root status and complete Location against the
serving deployment before attaching the public route. Every native response
carries `x-tuturuuu-runtime: native` for route readback, including redirects,
static assets and errors.

### Request reader qualification

Use `@tuturuuu/start-bridge/request-context/reader` for request readers without
store installation. The legacy `/core` entry retains the explicit installer
export; server request-context bootstrapping remains unchanged. Reader graph
tests cover local static/dynamic imports, forbidden installer edges and computed
imports. They do not qualify external package graphs.

The opt-in `@tuturuuu/start-bridge/vite/client-provenance` plugin belongs only in
a client build environment. It rejects request-store modules, async_hooks,
unresolved computed imports and external modules without transformed evidence.
Its receipt binds transformed modules and emitted chunks to SHA-256 digests.
Unit hook tests do not establish emitted artifact acceptance: exact-commit CI
must run the real client build with the plugin and retain its receipt. Existing
build and cutover gates remain required.

### Synthetic Linux isolation probes

`scripts/acceptance-fixture/launcher.py` is a nonshipping, fixed-target canary
launcher. It accepts no production endpoint or credentials and stops on macOS.
Its portable tests cover refusal and timeout control flow; Linux namespace and
teardown acceptance require a separately admitted Linux host. Read the fixture
README for host-mount and source-mutation limits. A `SYNTHETIC_ONLY` result does
not qualify an application runtime or establish a production exploit.
